text:
ana: heads-up — ran into a tenant burst that exposed fragmentation cliffs on host staging this morning. latency spikes ~3x for short seqs when offload kicks in. looking for quick tradeoffs before we lock the allocator API.

devin: ugh. can you paste the profile? which allocator/arena?

ana: it was the new segmented arena prototype (seg-arenas v2). pattern: many small transient tensors interleaved with a few long-lived KV cache items. we saw sudden resident set growth + PM evicts.

ana: snippet from the profiler:
```
allocs: small(64B-4KB)=heavy
long-lived: kv-cache (90MB)
evictors: host-staging on every 200ms window
latency_p50: 18ms -> 54ms
latency_p95: 112ms -> 310ms
```

maia: did we try compact-on-evict for the small chain? iirc seg-arenas didn't support compaction yet.

sam: correct — seg-arenas v2 chose no-compaction to keep O(1) alloc/free and minimal lock contention. thought soft compaction + background worker could be a follow-up.

devin: tradeoff: compaction reduces fragmentation but adds background CPU + pin windows which increase host staging churn. For tenant bursts, synchronous compaction hurts latency, async compaction risks repeated evicts.

riju: what about a hybrid: cooperative shrink API exposed to runtime that lets per-tenant schedulers suggest which arenas to sweep, with a contract like `shrink_hint(arena_id, target_free_bytes)`? then we can rate-limit compaction while keeping alloc path cheap.

ana: sketch of the API we discussed:
```
// runtime -> allocator
shrink_hint(arena_id: u64, target_free_bytes: usize, deadline_ms: u32) -> hint_ack

// allocator -> runtime (async)
shrink_progress(arena_id: u64, reclaimed_bytes: usize)
```

maia: would need to be tenant-aware: prioritize reclaim in arenas serving the noisy tenant to avoid cross-tenant tail latency. also add `hard_quota` and `burst_reserve` flags so we don't over-compact and starve long-lived tensors.

sam: also consider kv-cache pinning. If we compact blindly we may force the KV cache back to GPU or cause re-fetches. propose we mark cache pages as "soft-pinned" so compaction prefers unrelated small objects.

devin: curious about metrics: ops-bot ran a probe overnight? @ops-bot can you post the experiment numbers for cooperative shrink vs noop?

ops-bot: experiment run 2419000000-2419000800:
- baseline (no compaction): avg reclaim per hour=0.0MB, p95 eviction latency=220ms
- async-cooperative-shrink (rate 50MB/s): avg reclaim per hour=450MB, p95 eviction latency=120ms
- sync-compaction-on-evict: avg reclaim per hour=1.6GB, p95 eviction latency=400ms
(see /infra/benchmarks/seg-arena-2419.csv)

riju: those numbers match intuition. async-coop gives best p95 with reasonable reclaimed bytes. sync compaction too costly for latency-sensitive paths.

ana: proposal for next steps:
1) add `shrink_hint` API to allocator (lightweight, nonblocking)
2) implement tenant-scoped cooperative sweeper that accepts hints and rate-limits compaction by tenant-quota
3) add soft-pin annotation for cache tensors to exclude from compaction unless under memory emergency
4) add observability (per-arena reclaimed, compaction time, compaction CPU) in console

maia: +1. also add a feature flag so Dedicated customers can opt into more aggressive compaction policies.

devin: nit: define failure modes. If compaction is starved and memory pressure persists, fallback to cross-tenant eviction with knobbed priority. we should also expose a metric that counts "compaction-induced page-ins" for the KV cache.

sam: implementer notes: keep lock-free fast path. shrink_hint should just enqueue metadata to a low-priority worker; worker does best-effort scans with time-slicing. aim to avoid full memcpy during normal operation — prefer slab consolidation and pointer bumping where possible.

ana: I'll write a short RFC with the API + instrumentation plan. can we ship a light prototype in staging next week? @devin @maia pls review.

devin: ok — I'll review and add microbench harness for bursty allocation patterns.

maia: I'll mock the console dashboards and add alerts for compaction CPU > 20% per node.

riju: I'll prototype soft-pinning semantics in the allocator and add unit tests for eviction ordering.

ana: thanks everyone. follow-up: RFC posted at /eng/runtime/rfcs/2419001111-shrink-hint.md (will link when up). :thumbsup:
